title: Backend Module and Route Registration
appliesTo: the module opens the wrong screen
the module is not where I put it
page tree in a module that should not have one
hints: A backend module is declared in the owning extension's Configuration/Backend/Modules.php, which returns an array keyed by module identifier. There is no registration call.

The keys of an entry are parent (the identifier of the module it sits under), access ("user", "admin", ...), path (the backend route it answers on), iconIdentifier, labels, aliases (former identifiers kept working), routes, and moduleData for the module's persisted per-user state.
routes maps a route name to a target of the form Controller::class . '::method'; the entry named _default is what the module opens with.

A module with no parent registers no route unless it declares standalone => true. ModuleRegistry passes over every first-level module that is not standalone when it builds the route collection, so nothing throws and nothing is logged: the path falls through to whatever else matches, and the backend renders another module. The core's own single top-level entry is the Dashboard, which carries that key.

hints.text: A parent can promote instead of the child declaring itself: appearance.promotesSingleSubmoduleToStandalone on a parent that has exactly one submodule makes that submodule the top-level entry and drops the parent. The core files Media that way. It is the parent-side form of the same thing, and standalone on the module itself is the one that holds on every covered major.

hints: position => ['after' => '*'] reaches the end only where more than one module claims it. The modules claiming it are collected and populated first, and the block that then moves them behind everything else runs only where the first of them is not also the last — so one such module is left where it was populated, which is early. A module with no position at all keeps its registration order, and a project package is registered after the core's, which is what "last" was being asked for.

inheritNavigationComponentFromMainModule => false is how a submodule stops inheriting its parent's navigation component. Without it a module under a parent that carries the page tree gets the page tree, whatever it is about. EXT:form sets it.

hints.text: labels is a translation domain, not a file path. typo3_translation_domain_lookup computes it for the XLF file the module's labels live in.
labels is the LLL:EXT: reference of the XLF file the module's labels live in, not a domain.

Configure a module shortcut with $moduleTemplate->getDocHeaderComponent()->setShortcutContext($routeIdentifier, $displayName, $arguments). The doc header creates and positions the ShortcutButton; do not add one to its button bar manually.
Build a module shortcut through $moduleTemplate->getDocHeaderComponent()->getButtonBar()->makeShortcutButton(), set its route identifier, display name and arguments, then add it to that button bar.

hints: After a module POST changes state, return a RedirectResponse with HTTP 303 status. The browser then follows with GET; HTTP 302 does not state that method change and can repeat the POST.

Configuration/Backend/Routes.php and AjaxRoutes.php declare backend routes outside a module, in the same declarative style. They are not registered alike: an AjaxRoutes.php entry is registered under its key with ajax_ in front of it, a Routes.php entry under the key itself. backend-routing-internals carries the three spellings that follow from it.

A module's controller answers with a response the module template renders: $this->moduleTemplateFactory->create($request), the variables assigned to it, then $view->renderResponse('<Directory>/<Template>') for the Fluid template below Resources/Private/Templates. It is the doc header, the module menu and the backend chrome the module sits in, so a response built any other way is a page outside the backend.

The module's persisted per-user state arrives on the request as the moduleData attribute, built from the moduleData key of the registration. set() changes the object alone: what writes it back for the next request is $backendUser->pushModuleData($moduleData->getModuleIdentifier(), $moduleData->toArray()), and a module that never calls it looks like one whose state is not persisted at all.
These are declarative files with no schema check behind them: a wrong key does not fail at boot, it fails when a user opens the module. Take the shape from a neighbouring extension.

title: Backend Route Options, Sub-Route Identifiers, and Navigation Inheritance
appliesTo: which module a request is in
hints: A route a module registers carries the module object in its module option; a route declared in Configuration/Backend/Routes.php or AjaxRoutes.php does not. Module::getDefaultRouteOptions() puts it on every route of the module, so that option is what says whether a route belongs to a module at all.

hints.text: ModuleResolver is what answers which module a request is in, and it reads three sources in order: the module option of the routed route, the module request attribute, then the module query parameter.

hints: The module's _default route is registered under the module identifier itself. Every other route of the module is registered as <module identifier>.<route name>, because ModuleRegistry adds the collection under the module identifier and a dot.

An Extbase module generates one route per controller action rather than taking a routes map, named <ControllerAlias>_<action>, so its sub-route identifiers read <module identifier>.<ControllerAlias>_<action>. Every one of them gets the module's own route options; there is no per-action entry to configure.

AbstractServiceProvider::configureBackendRoutes() registers every Configuration/Backend/AjaxRoutes.php entry under 'ajax_' and the key the file writes, prefixes /ajax to the path it declares, and sets the ajax option the route is later collected by.

So one AJAX route is spelled three ways and only the URL builder's spelling carries the prefix. The key in AjaxRoutes.php is page_tree_data, buildUriFromRoute('ajax_page_tree_data') builds its URL, and JavaScript reads TYPO3.settings.ajaxUrls.page_tree_data, because PageRenderer::addAjaxUrlsToInlineSettings() strips the prefix off again for that array. Each of the three fails at runtime when it is written wrong, and the file that looks wrong is the one that is right.
Configuration/Backend/Routes.php has no such asymmetry. Its entries are merged under the keys the file writes, so buildUriFromRoute() takes exactly the key that stands there.

navigationComponent is inherited from the parent module unless the registration turns it off with inheritNavigationComponentFromMainModule, so a module's own Modules.php does not say whether it is page-tree navigated. Reading the registration files alone gives the wrong answer for every module that inherits.

TYPO3\CMS\Backend\Routing\Route takes a path and an options array; TYPO3\CMS\Core\Routing\Route takes a path, defaults, requirements and then options. Passing backend route options to the core class puts them where defaults belong, getOption() returns null with no error, and a test built that way asserts nothing.

title: Which Side of a Backend Module Resolves a Resource
hints: A backend module's TypeScript holds the editor's own state, and the identifiers and endpoint URLs its own PHP handed it. Which server-side resource a UI concept stands for is resolved by the controller.

The core's modules are built that way throughout. <typo3-backend-icon identifier="actions-close"> names an icon and never a file: IconController::getIcon() resolves the identifier through IconFactory, and the client's fallback for one that does not resolve is another identifier, default-not-found. The element browser is opened with a mode, and ElementBrowserRegistry::getElementBrowser() resolves the class behind it, throwing exception 1647241086 where nothing is registered under that name.

Carrying a resource path is not the same as deciding one. Option values the module's initial data supplied and the form submits back unchanged are the client carrying what the server gave it. A literal path, a suffix match on a file name, or a mapping from a UI mode to a resource is the client deciding, and the deciding is the half that belongs on the other side.

The controller resolves and validates such a value on arrival whatever the client sent, so a client that works the same answer out again buys nothing. FormManagerController::createAction() matches the submitted templatePath against the same newFormTemplates configuration getFormManagerAppInitialData() put into the module's payload, and throws a FormException — exception 1329233410 — where it does not appear there.

hints.text: The form manager is where the core breaks this itself: form-manager/view-model.ts sets templatePath to a literal EXT:form/Resources/Private/Backend/Templates/FormEditor/Yaml/NewForms/BlankForm.yaml for its blank mode, and that is the only literal EXT: resource path in the whole backend TypeScript tree.

No backend TypeScript source resolves a resource by path any more. The form manager was the last one, and the wizard rewrite dropped its hardcoded blank-form template rather than moving it into the payload the module is handed; the only EXT: reference left in the tree is an LLL: label key inside a Fluid title attribute.

hints: backend-typescript answers what builds the source and where its unit tests go. This one answers what the built module may decide.
